papers.title: OpenGCUA: Toward a Fully Open Stack for Generalist Computer Use
papers.summary: OpenGCUA introduces an open generalist computer-use agent that integrates visual and programmatic interfaces, harness-to-model decision transfer, and code execution to improve task performance and efficiency across models.

papers.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
papers.summary: FDE-Gym evaluates AI agents on realistic customer delivery tasks requiring clarification of ambiguous requirements and discovery of unstated constraints, revealing a substantial performance gap compared to well-specified benchmarks.

papers.title: MAI-Gym: An Open All-in-One Platform for GUI Agent Evaluation and RL Training across Mobile and Computer Environments
papers.summary: MAI-Gym is an open platform that unifies GUI agent evaluation, data collection, and online reinforcement learning training across mobile, computer, and web environments, enabling scalable synthesis of verified tasks and training of a unified 9B agent with state-of-the-art open performance.

papers.title: Can World and Action Modeling Benefit Each Other under Unified Causal Training?
papers.summary: OneWM unifies causal training of world and action modeling, showing that learning action-conditioned dynamics improves policies and action learning improves multi-view world prediction.

papers.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
papers.summary: A graded visual verifier decomposes complex multimodal rules into pointwise scores and uses decoupled reinforcement learning to improve generalization, with pairwise verification further enhancing structured world-modeling accuracy.

papers.title: Data World: Scaling Data Environments from Scratch
papers.summary: A multi-agent engine synthesizes data environments and tasks to train models for analytical insight discovery, improving performance across benchmarks without trajectory distillation.

papers.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
papers.summary: CoDA co-evolves a simulation engine and robot policy via shared memory of failures and progress, using vision-language diagnostics and staged potential rewards to improve out-of-distribution manipulation success.

papers.title: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture
papers.summary: SUPRA-Tex decouples visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and 3D completion to generate relightable 3D materials that preserve reference image details and complete unobserved surfaces.

papers.title: FlashMask-3: Efficient and Expressive Mask-Aware Distributed Attention
papers.summary: FlashMask-3 accelerates long-context attention via a Hopper-optimized sparse-mask kernel and distributed context-parallel extensions that eliminate mask-communication overhead and improve training throughput.

papers.title: Virtual Head Attention
papers.summary: Virtual Head Attention improves long-context model efficiency by reducing KV cache and compute while preserving quality through lightweight linear query and output transformations.

papers.title: SERO: Learning from Executable Oracle Continuations for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: SERO improves long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning by training on executable oracle continuations from real policy states, weighted by policy compatibility, without inference-time overhead.

papers.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
papers.summary: LEASH is a training-free framework that uses latent uncertainty to escalate from a weak to a strong computer-use agent only when needed and monitors the strong agent afterward, reducing cost while maintaining high success.

papers.title: LeanPRM: Lean-Grounded Process Supervision for Natural Language Proof Verification
papers.summary: LeanPRM uses the Lean proof assistant to automatically generate step-level correctness labels for natural-language mathematical proofs, enabling scalable training of learned verifiers without human annotation.

papers.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
papers.summary: Copy-Paste Language Models enhance in-context copying by adding a lightweight head that improves training efficiency, downstream performance, and long-context retrieval with minimal overhead.

papers.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
papers.summary: Gen4P repurposes a pretrained video generator into a feed-forward 4D perceiver that predicts geometry and motion from monocular video via on-demand cross-attention decoding and frozen depth priors.

papers.title: Behavioral Compositionality of Sparse Autoencoder Representations
papers.summary: Sparse autoencoder features are partially compositional but require interaction terms for accurate behavioral predictions and steering.

papers.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
papers.summary: PathFM is a trajectory-based forecasting model using flow matching to generate complete future paths, enabling efficient multi-path sampling and improved dependence modeling for time series.

papers.title: Explaining the Roles of Experts in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Personalization
papers.summary: Personalizing sparse Mixture-of-Experts language models enables localized, interpretable control over user-specific behaviors through specialized expert routing and learned personalized latents.

papers.title: Beyond Policy Rollouts: Embedding-Space Directional Exploration with Anchored Noise for LLM RLVR
papers.summary: EDEN improves reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by injecting anchored embedding noise into rollout conditioning to increase diversity and strengthen group-relative advantage signals without altering inference.

papers.title: Scalable Weak-to-Strong Verifier Hardening for Agent Environments
papers.summary: The study proposes an automated weak-to-strong loop that hardens agent environment verifiers against reward hacking by iteratively finding and repairing vulnerabilities in isolated sandboxes.

papers.title: Equal CER, Unequal Damage: Severity-Weighted Character Error Rate for OCR
papers.summary: A new metric called semCER uses an LLM judge to weight grapheme edits by severity, improving alignment with human ratings over standard character error rate for OCR and vision-language models.

papers.title: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
papers.summary: Hidden states encode task information before the readout expresses it, so behavioral timelines reflect readout learning rather than model acquisition, and faster readout training closes this gap earlier.

papers.title: One Bias Score, Two Factors: How Mitigations Affect Option Bias in Multiple-Choice Evaluation
papers.summary: Selection bias and order sensitivity in multiple-choice models are decomposed into flip rate and positional skew via pooled standard deviation, showing that prior correction and aggregation target different factors and should be reported together with accuracy.

papers.title: When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill
papers.summary: Remote KV caching for long-context LLM serving can severely degrade latency unless the store is sharded by parallel rank, loaded asynchronously, and paired with high-bandwidth retrieval, yielding large throughput gains.

papers.title: Speech event detector: Timestamped detection of non-verbal vocalizations and background sounds for rich speech transcription
papers.summary: A convolutional-Transformer model detects 54 speech and background event classes with timestamped outputs merged into transcripts, trained on unified multi-source annotations with synthetic augmentation.

papers.title: ForcingBooster: Adaptive Patch-wise Denoising for Fast Autoregressive Video Diffusion
papers.summary: A framework dynamically assigns denoising steps to video patches based on difficulty, cutting computation by half while preserving quality.

papers.title: SimForcing: Distilling Simulation Motion Priors into Real-Domain Robot World Models
papers.summary: SimForcing improves action-conditioned robot world models by distilling motion knowledge from simulation and using controllable simulation conditioning to generate realistic videos across robot datasets.

papers.title: CoWorld Reasoner: Agentic Multimodal Reasoning with the Evolving Video World Model-Driven Harness
papers.summary: CoWorld Reasoner is an agentic framework that uses a video world model as a flexible visual reasoning engine, enabling vision-language models to perform diverse spatiotemporal reasoning through guided visual imagination and co-evolving tools.

papers.title: Diminishing Returns of Data in Sparse Autoencoders: Functional Behavior does not Guarantee Feature Reproducibility
papers.summary: Sparse autoencoders can be trained with far fewer activation tokens when data budgets align with evaluation goals, though feature-level reproducibility demands larger scales.

papers.title: PAIR: Bridging Perception and Action in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.summary: PAIR introduces a shared perception-action representation via masked action autoencoders and bridge tokens to improve continuous-action vision-language-action models.
